full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the pre-emptee directed against the judgment and order No.26 dated 21-6-87 passed by Assistant Judge, Dumuria, District Khulna in Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1986. 

 2. The opposite party a pre-emptor filed case under section 96 of EBSA and Tenancy Act in the Court of Assistant Judge, being Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1986 on 11-8-86 against the present petitioner and other opposite parties. Said Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1986 was decreed ex parte on 11-12-86. Thereafter the pre-emptee petitioner filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of Civil Procedure Code which is the subject-matter of Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1986 on 27-12-86 alleging, inter alia, that the show cause notice and registered notice of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1986 were not duly served upon him which were suppressed in collusion with the process server and thereby the pre-empter who in collusion with the process server and the simultaneous issue of registered letter under Order 5 rule 19B was not received by the petitioner rather received by one Nur Mohammad who is own man of the pre-emptor. The petitioner came to know the said miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1986 from one Asaduzzaman only on 23-12-86 at his residence and thereafter learnt about the Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1986 and the ex parte decree; accordingly filed the Misc. Case No. 83 of 1986 under Order 9 rule 13 CPC for setting aside the ex parte decree on 27-12-86 well within 30 days. The certified copy of the said petition and Misc. Case No.83 of 1986 is made annexure C of this petition and certified copy of show cause notice with service return is filed as Annexure-D of this petition. 

 3. The present opposite party No.1 appeared in this Misc. Case No. 83 of 1986 and filed written objection on 25-2-87 denying all the allegations of the petitioner alleging due service and further asserting that Mokabila witness regarding service of show cause notice are relative of petitioner. It was also asserted that registered letter was duly served. The certified copy of said written objection is filed as annexure E of this petition. But he did not appear at the hearing of miscellaneous case. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge by the impugned order rejected the said miscellaneous case. 

 5. Mr. MA Jabbar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the opposite party No.1 has failed to discharge his onus to prove service inasmuch mokabila witness deposed denying service. and there was an initial error regarding service in the absence of non-examination of process server by the court before recording due service of notice upon the party and on the same day the case was set for ex parte hearing on 1-12-86. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the fact that the service was under rule 17 of Order 5 the court has a duty to ascertain by enquiry as to whether summon has been duly served or not. 

 7. It appears from the order sheet of the Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1986 that the case was filed on 11-8-1986 and 20-8-1986 was fixed for filing challan, on 20-8-86 notices of the case was ordered to be issued upon the opposite parties fixing 5-11-1986 for return and on that date that case was adjourned to 12-11-86 for return of AID, on 12-11-86 the court recorded the order as under; 

 on 1-12-1986 the petitioner therein prayed for time and the case was adjourned to 11-12-1986 for ex parte hearing, on 11-12-1986 the case was heard and decreed ex parte. 

 8. The relevant provisions regarding service of summons notices involved in this case are rules 17, 19 and 19A of Order V of CPC. In view of the service of notice under rule 17 Court has a duty to examine the serving officer on oath touching his proceeding and to ascertain by enquiry in the matter as to whether the summons have been duly served or not and declare that the summons/notices have been served. Rule 19A thereof goes to show that any declaration by the process server should be received as a piece of evidence on making necessary inquiry by examining the process server on oath or making any such further enquiry. 

 9. In the case of Johara Begum vs. Rafiqul Kader 25 DLR 91 it has been held that Rule 19A cannot be read to take away the responsibility of the court as provided in Rule 19, nor can it be read to justify recording in the order sheet as a matter of routine that summons was duly served. 

 10. In the case of Santosh Kumar Chakraborty and ors vs. MA Motaleb Hossain & on, 36 DLR AD 248 it has been held that it was incumbent upon the court to make an enquiry and to record a declaration of due service in spite of the fact that the return accompanied a declaration as to service in which case the examination of the process server is not mandatory. 

 12. In the instant case the learned Munsif having recorded in his order dated 12-11-86 that নোটিশ জারী হয় is not the requirement of law as to due service of notice and, as such, there was no due service of notice in the case. 

 13. Accordingly, the learned Munsif erred in law in fixing the case for ex parte hearing by the same order dated 12-11-86 and disposing of the case ex parte by order dated 11-12-86 is illegal and, as such, the said impugned order is liable to be set aside and accordingly the same is set aside as the same was passed in the absence of any due service of notice upon the petitioner. 

 14. The pre-emptor has claimed pre-emption in respect of kabala dated 1-6-86 and the alleged transfer was effected on 21-12-1986 even after the ex parte decree dated 11-12-86. The ex parte decree dated 11-12-1986 has been impugned in this proceeding and the pre-emptee had interest in the case which accrued on' 11-12-1986 and, as such, even after transfer on 21-12-86 the pre-emptee petitioner has a right to proceed with the ex parte decree and as such the case is maintainable and the proceeding under Order 9 rule 13 CPC do not become infructuous by the alleged transfer on 21-12-1986. 

 15. In view of the above, the impugned judgment and order dated 21-6-87 passed by the learned Assistant Judge are set aside and the Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1986 is hereby allowed and the Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1986 is restored to its original file and number setting aside the exparte decree dated 11-12-86.
